spec_family.name: Exterior Foundation Wall Coating
spec_family.description: Above-grade exposed foundation wall coating for new construction. Covers moisture testing (MC <= 4% hard stop), form-release agent removal (poured concrete), efflorescence treatment, surface profiling, block filler (CMU), alkali-resistant primer, and finish coating (acrylic or cementitious). Uses SF as primary UOM. Typically a small add-on line item — foundation band is 12-36 inches tall with limited surface area. CRITICAL: Never caulk the 3/8-inch grade-line gap below siding — it is an intentional drainage plane.

includes: Moisture testing (MC <= 4% hard stop — stricter than masonry wall 12%)
Form-release agent and laitance removal (poured concrete only)
Bug hole and form-tie patching (poured concrete only)
Surface profile verification (CSP 1-2 for thin cosmetic coating)
Block filler application for CMU foundation (PCA P12 Level 2)
Alkali-resistant primer (mandatory on ALL new foundation — pH 12-14)
Finish coat application — acrylic (1-2 coats by QT) or cementitious/Drylok-type (1-2 coats by QT)
Landscape perimeter protection (LF-based along foundation base)

excludes.item: Below-grade waterproofing (40-60 mils DFT, sheet membrane, bituminous systems)
excludes.route_to: Specialty waterproofing trade — not painting contractor scope
Framing trade — not painting contractor scope
GC / structural engineer — flag and stop

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling coat count, cleaning intensity, inspection scrutiny, and defect tolerance.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT2=economy (light wash, primer, single finish coat — budget-appropriate for utilitarian foundation). QT3=standard (full wash, efflorescence treatment, primer, two finish coats — higher-end residential where foundation appearance matters). No QT4/QT5 — foundation is utilitarian, not decorative. All tiers require alkali-resistant primer (pH hazard is not quality-optional).

configuration_dimensions.description: Foundation substrate type. Drives block filler requirement (CMU only), surface prep branching (form-release removal for poured, void filling for CMU), roller nap selection, and production rate modifier.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Poured concrete is smooth with potential form-release agents, laitance, and bug holes. CMU has open-cell voids requiring block filler before coating. Both are cementitious substrates classified under SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY.

configuration_dimensions.description: Finish coating material category for above-grade foundation.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Acrylic: 100% acrylic exterior masonry paint — wider color range, UV-resistant, flat or satin sheen. Cementitious (Drylok-type): fills pores, breathable, matte/flat only, excellent adhesion to concrete, budget-friendly, withstands 15 PSI hydrostatic pressure. Elastomeric is excluded — overkill for above-grade cosmetic foundation coating.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for prime and finish coats.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Roll is the typical primary method for small foundation bands. Spray for larger continuous runs on smooth poured concrete — spray-only IS valid on foundation (unlike masonry walls where backroll is mandatory). Brush for detail work around pipes/vents. CMU foundation with spray SHOULD include backroll per masonry doctrine (handled as conditional task, not separate method enum).

paintable_items.name: Exterior Above-Grade Foundation Wall Surface
paintable_items.counting_rules: Net paintable above-grade foundation wall area in square feet. Typically perimeter LF x band height (12-36 inches). Excludes below-grade surfaces. Measured from PaintScope.
paintable_items.notes: Single paintable item. Covers both poured concrete and CMU foundation surfaces. Foundation_type modifier adjusts prep sequence and material requirements per substrate type.

valid_input_states.notes: SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY is the single NC state for both poured concrete and CMU foundation. Both are cementitious substrates with pH 12-14. No factory-primed foundation exists. Alkali-resistant primer mandatory.

output_state.notes: Foundation coating is flat sheen. Cementitious coatings are inherently matte/flat. Acrylic on foundation is also typically flat for utilitarian surface.

material_systems.name: Alkali-Resistant Foundation Primer
material_systems.notes: MANDATORY on ALL new foundation regardless of quality tier. pH 12-14 requires alkali-resistant primer (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer rated to pH 13). Enables 7-day accelerated coating vs 28-day standard cure. Oil-based primer PROHIBITED — saponification on alkaline concrete is catastrophic.

material_systems.name: Block Filler for CMU Foundation (PCA P12 Level 2)
material_systems.notes: Mandatory for CMU foundation. Fills open-cell voids to PCA P12 Level 2 standard (max 10 voids per SF). Heavy-body product requiring 527-535 spray tip and 30-mesh filter. Applied BEFORE primer. Not quality-optional — required at all tiers.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Foundation Coating
material_systems.notes: 100% acrylic exterior masonry paint. UV-resistant. 10-20 perms breathability. QT2 single coat, QT3 two coats on primed surface. Wider color range than cementitious.

material_systems.name: Cementitious Coating for Foundation (Drylok-type)
material_systems.notes: Cementitious/crystalline coating (e.g., Drylok, UGL). Fills pores, breathable, matte finish only. Withstands 15 PSI hydrostatic pressure. Thicker application (10-15 mils DFT) than acrylic — lower coverage rate (150-200 SF/gal). Budget-friendly material cost.

modules.notes: Moisture test (MC <= 4% hard stop), form-release removal (poured only), efflorescence treatment, pressure wash, crack patch, bug hole patch (poured only), surface profile
Block filler spray or roll — CMU only (PCA P12)
Finish coats — acrylic (spray/roll) or cementitious (roll/brush) + brush detail

production_summary.notes: Single modifier — FAC_FNDN_FOUNDATION_TYPE only. No access modifier (ground-level), no coating system modifier, no QT modifier (only 2 tiers). Maximum stack is 1.15x — well under 4.0x cap. Simplest modifier profile of any exterior spec.

protection_zones_required.notes: LF-based — measured along foundation wall base where landscape is adjacent. Drop cloth at base for roll/brush. Full tarp over plantings for spray (10-15 ft overspray drift at ground level).
Adjacent walkways at foundation base. Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic. Full tarp for spray overspray.
Adjacent patio surfaces. Protection level driven by proximity and application method.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Net paintable above-grade foundation wall area
Foundation substrate type (poured/CMU) — drives block filler, prep sequence, production modifier
Boolean flag confirming new construction context. Always true for this NC spec.

required_paintscope_inputs.required_when: When landscape is adjacent to foundation wall
required_paintscope_inputs.description: Linear feet of foundation perimeter where landscape is adjacent and requires protection

required_paintscope_inputs.required_when: When walkways are adjacent to foundation wall
When patio is adjacent to foundation wall

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Siding meets foundation at grade line with 3/8-inch gap and Z-flashing. Foundation coating terminates below siding edge. No cut-in required — the gap provides a natural break. NEVER caulk this gap.
Foundation meets grade (soil/mulch/gravel). Coating extends to grade line or slightly below. No edge precision needed — rough termination at soil line is acceptable.
Water table trim (if present) sits at siding-to-foundation transition. Foundation coating terminates below water table. Separate trim spec.

adjacency_declarations.key_finding: Foundation wall has NO edge work requirements within this spec. The grade-line gap at siding provides a natural termination. Soil/grade provides a rough bottom edge. No precision cut-in needed anywhere. Simplest adjacency profile of any exterior spec.

boundaries.notes: Siding protection above foundation is NOT this spec's responsibility — belongs in siding spec.
Below-grade waterproofing (40-60 mils DFT) is specialty trade, not painting contractor scope.
Wind, dew point, surface temperature are scheduling/process concerns. Not estimatable at bid time.

cross_spec_coordination.notes: Foundation is an isolated low-interaction spec. No cross-spec flags needed. Siding protection above foundation belongs in siding spec, not here.

compatibility_rules.description: Oil-based and alkyd products PROHIBITED on alkaline concrete/CMU foundation
compatibility_rules.notes: Alkaline hydroxides (pH 12-14) react with alkyd/oil paint esters through saponification — hydrolyzing binder into soft, sticky, water-soluble soap. Complete removal to bare substrate is the only remedy.

compatibility_rules.description: Moisture content must be at or below 4% before any coating
compatibility_rules.required_action: Moisture test with electronic meter at multiple points. MC > 4% = HARD STOP
compatibility_rules.notes: Stricter than masonry wall spec (12%) due to continuous ground contact and capillary moisture rise through foundation.

compatibility_rules.description: NEVER caulk the 3/8-inch grade-line gap below siding
compatibility_rules.notes: The grade-line gap with Z-flashing is an intentional drainage plane. Caulking seals the drainage path, trapping moisture behind siding — causes catastrophic rot, mold, and structural damage. #1 grade-line failure mode. Mask the gap during painting, do not fill it.

compatibility_rules.description: Concrete Surface Profile (CSP) must match coating thickness
compatibility_rules.required_action: CSP 1-2 for thin cosmetic coatings (<10 mils DFT). 83% of foundation coating failures originate from insufficient surface roughness.
compatibility_rules.notes: Above-grade cosmetic coating requires CSP 1-2 (smooth to light profile). For poured concrete, form-release removal achieves adequate CSP.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 1 Finish Coat (Poured Concrete, QT2)
round_configurations.notes: QT2 economy. Single finish coat on properly primed poured concrete. Acceptable for utilitarian foundation band.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 2 Finish Coats (Poured Concrete, QT3)
round_configurations.notes: QT3 standard. Two finish coats for higher-end residential. No interstage sanding — utilitarian surface.

round_configurations.name: Block Filler + Prime + 1 Finish Coat (CMU, QT2)
round_configurations.notes: QT2 economy CMU. Block filler is phase=prep (substrate preparation, not a coating). 3 total applied layers: filler + primer + 1 finish.

round_configurations.name: Block Filler + Prime + 2 Finish Coats (CMU, QT3)
round_configurations.notes: QT3 standard CMU. 4 total applied layers: filler + primer + 2 finish. No interstage sanding.

variants.notes: Economy poured concrete, acrylic roll. Most common budget foundation coating. Primer + 1 finish coat.
Standard poured concrete, acrylic roll. Primer + 2 finish coats. Showcase foundation.
Standard poured concrete, acrylic spray. Fastest production for long continuous foundation runs. Spray-only IS valid on smooth poured concrete.
Economy poured concrete, Drylok-type. Budget-friendly cementitious coating. Single coat.
Standard poured concrete, Drylok-type. Two finish coats for moisture-prone foundation areas.
Economy CMU, acrylic roll. Block filler + primer + 1 finish coat. Block filler mandatory on CMU.
Standard CMU, acrylic roll. Block filler + primer + 2 finish coats.
Standard CMU, Drylok-type. Block filler + primer + 2 cementitious finish coats. Highest material consumption variant.

risk_flags.description: Caulking the 3/8-inch siding-to-foundation gap seals the drainage plane. Moisture trapped behind siding causes rot, mold, and structural damage. This damages the building structure, not just the coating.
risk_flags.mitigation: NEVER caulk the siding-to-foundation gap. Mask the gap during painting. Educate homeowner/GC that the gap is intentional drainage. SOP hard stop.

risk_flags.description: Foundation MC > 4% at coating surface will cause coating failure — osmotic blistering, delamination, efflorescence migration through film. Foundation walls have continuous ground contact with capillary moisture rise.
risk_flags.mitigation: Electronic moisture meter test at multiple points. MC > 4% = HARD STOP. Do not coat. Wait, re-test. Stricter than masonry wall (12%).

risk_flags.description: Poured concrete retains waxy/oily form-release agents. Coating applied over form-release agents will peel off in sheets within weeks.
risk_flags.mitigation: Clean with TSP/degreaser. Wire brush to remove laitance and form-release residue. Water bead test to verify removal. Tape test adhesion check before full application.

risk_flags.description: Oil-based or alkyd paints on alkaline foundation (pH 12-14) undergo saponification — irreversible chemical destruction of the binder. Complete removal to bare concrete is the only remedy.
risk_flags.mitigation: Use ONLY water-based acrylic or cementitious products. Alkali-resistant primer (SYS_EXT_FNDN_PRIMER_ALKALI) mandatory. Material system blocker rule COMPAT-FNDN-001.

risk_flags.description: Coating over active efflorescence traps salt migration path. Salts accumulate behind coating film creating osmotic pressure blisters. Foundation is particularly susceptible due to ground contact.
risk_flags.mitigation: Remove ALL efflorescence before coating. Verify MC <= 4%. Do not coat foundation with active moisture migration.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Setup -> Prep -> Block Fill (CMU only) -> Prime -> Finish (1-2 coats by QT) -> Final Inspect -> Cleanup
sequencing_notes.edge_work: No edge work in this spec. Grade-line gap provides natural siding termination. Soil line provides rough bottom edge. No precision cut-in needed anywhere.
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Landscape perimeter protection -> Hardscape walk/patio (if adjacent) -> Coating work -> Protection teardown -> Equipment cleanup
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence: Moisture test (HARD STOP if MC >4%) -> Prep (form-release, efflorescence, wash, patch, profile) -> Block filler (CMU only) -> Prime (alkali-resistant) -> Finish 1 -> Finish 2 (QT3 only) -> Final inspect -> Touch up
sequencing_notes.key_prohibitions: NO caulking the grade-line gap. NO oil-based or alkyd products. NO coating at MC >4%. NO QT4/QT5. NO elastomeric (overkill for foundation).

relationships.cross_spec_protection_note: Siding protection above foundation is NOT this spec's responsibility — belongs in siding spec. Foundation is a LOW protection spec with 3 exterior zones.
relationships.notes: Smaller sibling of masonry wall spec. Key departures from masonry: QT2-QT3 only (no QT4), no access modifier (ground-level only), MC 4% (not 12%), spray-only IS valid (no mandatory backroll on poured concrete), no elastomeric option, cementitious coating option (not in masonry spec), 2 substrate types (not 4), single modifier (not 4). Combined prime+finish in single mobilization.

sections_used: Ground-level access — no height modifier for foundation

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for exterior above-grade foundation wall coating (poured concrete and CMU). Small add-on scope — foundation band 12-36 inches above grade. Key features: combined prime+paint (single mobilization), single NC substrate state (SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY), 2 foundation types (poured/CMU), 2 coating systems (acrylic/cementitious), 3 application methods (spray/roll/brush — spray-only valid on foundation unlike masonry walls), flat sheen only, 2 quality tiers (QT2-QT3, QT4/QT5 excluded — utilitarian surface), 24 tasks across 7 modules (incl. block fill module for CMU), 4 material systems (1 specialty + 1 primer + 2 finish), 1 factor modifier (foundation_type only — no access/QT/coating modifiers), 4 round configurations, 8 variants. 4 compatibility rules enforce foundation-specific constraints (oil-based prohibition, MC 4% hard stop, grade-line gap never caulked, CSP match). 5 risk flags (3 critical, 2 major). Ground-level access only — no height modifier. Sibling of SF_MASONRY_EXT_NC with significant simplification.
